The upcoming change was destined to cram `toE164`, `normalizeTelephone`, and `rejectDuplicateTelephone` all into `OwnerRestControllerV1`, overloading it. I gave telephone handling its own home first, so the change can land there instead of in the controller.

**New file — `util/TelephoneNormalizer.java`**
A stateless helper modeled on the codebase's existing `EntityUtils` (abstract class, static methods, no web/persistence dependencies). It holds the two pure telephone primitives:
- `normalize(String)` → the canonical stored form (currently strip-to-digits + require exactly 10), returning `Optional.empty()` when invalid. This is the seam the `toE164` conversion algorithm will grow into.

The original dedup stripped stored values **without** re-validating length — reachable because `updateOwner` sets telephone without normalization — so folding both into one validating function would have silently changed that edge case. Routing the submitted value (already 10 digits) through `toComparisonKey` is idempotent, and the `DuplicateOwnerTelephoneException` still carries the original `normalizedTelephone`, so the 400/409 responses and messages are unchanged. Seed telephones are all 10-digit, so nothing shifts there either.
